title: Why Leah Kept Naming Sons
paragraphs:
Why Leah Kept Naming Sons
The woman who was never chosen… but never stopped hoping
They never told her she was the consolation prize.

No one said it out loud when her father led her into that tent in the dark, when the veil covered more than her face, when deception sealed a marriage that was never supposed to be hers. But Leah felt it the moment morning came and love did not follow.
Scripture doesn’t soften it. It doesn’t try to protect her dignity from the rawness of truth.

“וַיַּרְא יְהוָה כִּי־שְׂנוּאָה לֵאָה”
“Vayar YHWH ki senu’ah Leah”
“And the LORD saw that Leah was hated.” (Genesis 29:31)

Not unloved in a mild way. Not overlooked politely. The Hebrew word שְׂנוּאָה (senu’ah) carries the weight of rejection, emotional abandonment, being set aside. Leah wasn’t just second… she was unwanted.
And yet, God saw her.
That’s where the story begins. Not with Jacob. Not with rivalry. But with divine attention falling on a woman nobody chose.
So God opened her womb.
And Leah did something that feels strange until you realize it’s exactly what we do too… she started naming her pain.
Her first son, she called Reuben.

“כִּי־רָאָה יְהוָה בְּעָנְיִי”
“Ki ra’ah YHWH b’onyi”
“Because the LORD has seen my affliction.” (Genesis 29:32)
Reuben… “See, a son.”
Can you hear it? She wasn’t just naming a child. She was speaking to the ache inside her chest.
Maybe now my husband will see me.
Maybe now I’ll be enough.
Maybe now I won’t feel invisible.
But Jacob didn’t change.
So she had another son.
Simeon.

“כִּי־שָׁמַע יְהוָה”
“Ki shama YHWH”
“Because the LORD has heard.” (Genesis 29:33)
If seeing didn’t fix it, maybe being heard will.
God hears me… but does he?
Does anyone?

Some of you reading this… you’ve been there. You’ve prayed, you’ve cried, you’ve tried to prove your worth in ways nobody ever asked you to. You keep hoping something will finally make you feel chosen.
But the silence keeps answering.
Leah wasn’t done.
She had a third son.
Levi.

“הַפַּעַם יִלָּוֶה אִישִׁי אֵלַי”
“Hapa’am yilaveh ishi elai”
“Now this time my husband will be attached to me.” (Genesis 29:34)
Do you feel the shift?
She’s no longer just naming what God did. She’s pleading through her naming.
This time…
This time he’ll stay.
This time I’ll matter.
This time I won’t feel alone.
But nothing changed.
And that’s the part we skip too quickly when we read her story. Because it’s uncomfortable to sit in a place where prayers seem unanswered and effort feels wasted. But Leah lived there.
Child after child.
Hope after disappointment.
Effort after silence.
Until something broke inside her… or maybe something finally healed.
Her fourth son.
Judah.

“הַפַּעַם אוֹדֶה אֶת־יְהוָה”
“Hapa’am odeh et YHWH”
“Now I will praise the LORD.” (Genesis 29:35)
No mention of Jacob.
No more bargaining.
No more “maybe now he will love me.”
Just… praise.
That word אוֹדֶה (odeh) comes from the root ידה (yadah), meaning to give thanks, to confess, to surrender acknowledgment. This wasn’t surface-level gratitude. This was a deep, soul-level release.
Leah stopped naming her pain based on what she hoped people would give her… and started naming her life based on what God already had.
And everything changed.
Not her circumstances.
Not Jacob’s affection.
Not her position.
But her center.
Because the moment she stopped chasing validation horizontally… she found identity vertically.
And here’s the part that should shake you.
Judah… the son born from surrender… becomes the lineage of Jesus Christ.

“βίβλος γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ… Ἰούδας”
“Biblos geneseos Iēsou Christou… Ioudas”
“The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ… Judah.” (Matthew 1:1–2)
Not Rachel.
Not the loved one.
Leah.
The rejected woman.
The overlooked wife.
The one who kept naming sons in the middle of heartbreak.
God didn’t just see her.
He wrote Himself into her story.
And maybe that’s why this hits harder than expected.
Because some of you are still in your “Reuben” season… trying to be seen.
Some of you are in your “Simeon” season… crying out to be heard.
Some of you are in your “Levi” season… hoping someone will finally stay.
But God is calling you into your “Judah” season.
Where praise isn’t dependent on people.
Where identity isn’t tied to approval.
Where your worth isn’t negotiated through performance.
Leah kept naming sons because she was searching for something every human soul craves… to be chosen.
And she found it… not in Jacob… but in God.
Be honest… this exposed something deeper than you expected, didn’t it?
Someone you love is still stuck in a cycle of trying to be enough for people who will never choose them. This could be the moment God uses to shift their entire life.
Follow closely if you’re serious about growing deeper in Christ… not surface faith, but real transformation, real surrender, real healing.

And if you truly want to glorify God through what you consume and support… stand with this mission. This isn’t just content… this is discipleship, this is restoration, this is souls being called back to Jesus.
Because at the end of everything… Leah’s story wasn’t about being unwanted.
It was about being chosen by the only One who truly matters.
And He is still choosing people like her… like you… like me.
The love you keep begging for from people was never meant to replace the love God already gave you.
